clue.text: Press opportunity to move over European statesman

parts.note: to press clothes is to iron them
a chance is an opportunity

indicators.note: over says the word for move is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: to roll is to move along by turning

explanation.surface: A statesman seizes a press opportunity before handing over to someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iron Chancellor was Otto von Bismarck, who unified Germany by 'blood and iron'.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname belongs to Bismarck, the Prussian leader who became Germany's first chancellor.

clue.text: Trendy drink reported in business — this can affect markets

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: reported means the drink's name is to be heard as spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: cider is an alcoholic drink made from apples
a company still trading is in business

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy on a fashionable drink lets slip something in a business deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description rather than a synonym: trading on confidential knowledge moves share prices, which is why it is illegal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealing in shares on confidential knowledge is illegal precisely because it distorts prices on stock exchanges.

clue.text: United States under old tyrant is oppressive

indicators.note: in a down answer, under places the US after the earlier letters

parts.note: Nero was the tyrannical Roman emperor

explanation.surface: The American nation suffering under an ancient tyrant finds life oppressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something burdensome and heavy to bear is onerous, a close synonym of oppressive.

clue.text: Parking in cover having a lot of small trees

definitions.text: having a lot of small trees

indicators.note: in puts the parking letter inside the word for cover

parts.note: a cosy is a cover, as in a tea cosy
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A car park tucked under cover in a wooded spot.
explanation.walkthrough: COPSY is an adjective from copse, a thicket of small trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small wood or thicket, so land full of copses is copsy.

clue.text: A fish together with a fish jelly

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish
gar again, the long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: Two fish served up together in a jelly, like an aspic dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar-agar is a gelatinous substance from seaweed, used as a setting agent in cooking and labs.

clue.text: Cutting about a hard religious leader

indicators.note: about puts the word for cutting round the A

parts.note: a clip is a cutting, as from a newspaper
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A newspaper cutting about a tough cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A caliph was the chief Muslim ruler, successor to Muhammad as head of the faith.

clue.text: Queen in shot with heads of Europe's nobles and even Maggie, for one?

indicators.note: in puts the Queen inside the rest of the letters

parts.note: lead shot is the pellets fired from a gun

indicators.note: heads of picks the first letters of the three following words

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen in a photo alongside European aristocrats and even Margaret Thatcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maggie' is Margaret Thatcher, the British Prime Minister nicknamed the Leaderene by Norman St John-Stevas.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaderene is a jocular term for a female leader, applied above all to Thatcher; the question mark marks her as one example.

clue.text: What's found in central Bolivia — one new mineral

indicators.note: central takes the middle letters of each of the three words: Bolivia less its ends, and the middle letter of one and of new

explanation.surface: A mineral discovered in the heart of Bolivia, one new find.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central' covers all three words: the middle of BOLIVIA is OLIVI, of ONE N, of NEW E.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivine is a green silicate of magnesium and iron, a common rock-forming mineral whose gem form is peridot.

clue.text: Ordinary coarse fish dive around men

indicators.note: around here loosely places men next to the fish and dive rather than inside them

parts.note: common means coarse or vulgar
OR, other ranks, is military shorthand for men as opposed to officers
a gar is a long-snouted fish
a den is a dive, a seedy haunt

explanation.surface: Coarse fishing for an ordinary fish: plunging round the men on the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coarse fish' looks like one phrase (anglers' term for freshwater fish other than trout and salmon) but splits in two. 'around' only loosely places the men beside the fish and dive.
explanation.definitionFit: Common-or-garden is an idiom for something everyday and unremarkable, like a plain garden plant.

clue.text: Observe daughter pressure nobleman for gem

parts.note: to see is to observe
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
P is the physics symbol for pressure
an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: Watch a daughter lean on an aristocrat to buy her a jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: A seed pearl is a very small pearl, used as a jewel in embroidery and jewellery.

clue.text: Friend's gone — I'm back inside

indicators.note: inside puts those reversed letters within the word for gone

parts.note: ago means gone by, past

indicators.note: back means the letters of I'm are read the other way

parts.note: I'm without the apostrophe gives the letters IM

explanation.surface: A friend has left, and I'm returning home.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for a pal, borrowed into English as a casual word for a mate.

clue.text: Something very good seen back in Dudley Zoo days

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters lie inside the words Dudley Zoo days

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A great outing remembered from days out at Dudley Zoo, a zoo in the English Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft folded 'seen' into the definition and left the hiding signal unnamed; 'in' is that signal, and 'seen' is only a link, so the definition is 'Something very good'.
explanation.definitionFit: A doozy is informal American slang for an outstanding or remarkable example of something.

clue.text: Trembling, as in plume fern

indicators.note: trembling suggests something shaken up, so the letters of as in plume are rearranged

explanation.surface: A frond quivering like a feather in a fern.
explanation.definitionFit: Asplenium is the botanical genus of spleenworts, a large group of ferns.

clue.text: Remaining exam taken again — with the time cut — in two parts

indicators.note: cut says one letter standing for time is removed from the exam word

parts.note: a resit is an exam taken a second time
dual means consisting of two parts

explanation.surface: A repeat exam, shortened and split into two papers, still remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Residual describes what is left over, the residue remaining after the rest has gone.

clue.text: Protestor to criticise distinctive TV feature

parts.note: to diss someone is to criticise them disrespectfully
an ident is a channel's identifying logo or short sequence on TV

explanation.surface: A protestor sets out to attack a television station's trademark feature.
explanation.walkthrough: An ident is the short branded clip or corner logo that identifies a TV channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissident openly opposes an established regime or policy, a political protestor.

clue.text: Composer's live recording originally taking place in large city

indicators.note: taking place in puts the live and recording letters inside the city word

parts.note: the Great Wen was Cobbett's disparaging name for London, so a wen is a large city
to be is to live, exist

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of recording

explanation.surface: A composer's live recording first made in a big city.
explanation.walkthrough: Anton Webern was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School.
explanation.definitionFit: Webern, pupil of Schoenberg, wrote spare twelve-tone music in early twentieth-century Vienna.

clue.text: United pea and tofu in blending soup

indicators.note: in blending says the letters are mixed together into a new order

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: Pea and tofu whizzed together in a blender make soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot-au-feu is a French dish of boiled meat and vegetables, its broth served as a soup.

clue.text: Calm grew outside European Parliament

indicators.note: outside means the word for grew goes round the parliament letters

parts.note: rose means grew or increased

explanation.surface: Tranquillity grew outside the European Parliament building.
explanation.definitionFit: Repose means rest or tranquillity, a state of being calm.

clue.text: Washed-out end to our month in Italian city

parts.note: washed-out colours are pale

indicators.note: end to picks the last letter of our

explanation.surface: A faded finish to our month's stay in an Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Palermo is the capital of Sicily, a city of southern Italy.

clue.text: First item of news on the radio?

definitions.text: First item of news on the radio?

parts.words: First item of news on the radio?
parts.note: the first letter of news is N, and radio operators say that letter with a code word from the phonetic alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a bulletin's lead story; 'on the radio' means the radio spelling alphabet, where N is spoken as NOVEMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO phonetic alphabet each letter has a code word, and the one for the letter N is a month's name.

clue.text: Rod's in bar with one car designer

indicators.note: in puts the gun word inside the word for bar

parts.note: but means bar, except, as in all but one
a rod and a gat are both slang for a gun, so rod is gat
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Rod is in the pub with one fellow who designs cars.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod and gat are both American gangster slang for a pistol; 'bar' means except.
explanation.definitionFit: Ettore Bugatti founded the French marque famous for luxury racing cars he designed.

clue.text: Chap hugging in the manner of greeting

indicators.note: hugging means the name wraps around the other letters

parts.note: Sam is a man's name, a chap
a la, from French, means in the manner of

explanation.surface: A man embracing someone in the style of a warm greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Salaam is an Arabic word for peace used as a salutation, often with a low bow.

clue.text: An African country with a youth backing religious leader

indicators.note: backing means the whole string of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: an gives the single letter A
Mali is a country in West Africa
a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A country in Africa and a young man supporting a religious leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support but reverses AMALIALAD in full.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dalai Lama is the spiritual head of Tibetan Buddhism.

clue.text: Letter removing tons from disgrace

indicators.note: removing says the tons letter is taken out of the disgrace word

parts.note: a stigma is a mark of disgrace

explanation.surface: A letter that clears a huge weight of shame.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the eighteenth character of the Greek alphabet, equivalent to S.

clue.text: Period of mourning for god

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., the seven days of Jewish mourning after a funeral
second meaning: ..., the Hindu god of destruction

explanation.walkthrough: Two unrelated words share the spelling: a Hebrew term for the mourning week and the name of the Hindu deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Jewish families sit shiva for seven days after a death; Shiva is also one of Hinduism's principal deities.

clue.text: Bottle just about right to be knocked back?

indicators.note: knocked back means the result is read the other way
about puts the fair word round the letter for right

parts.note: even means just, fair

explanation.surface: A bottle that's barely right for downing in one gulp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' suggests a drink to knock back, but it is British slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle is British slang for courage, and nerve is the same steady boldness.

clue.text: Harassed following force when protected by rocky citadel

indicators.note: protected by means the two letters sit inside the rearranged citadel
rocky means unsteady, so the letters of citadel are shaken into a new order

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: Pursued under fire, the troops are harassed while sheltering in an unsteady fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: Afflicted means troubled or distressed, close to being harassed and tormented.

clue.text: Idea about funny cat album is moving when not self-aware

indicators.note: about means the idea word wraps round the rearranged letters

parts.note: a notion is an idea

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the letters of cat album are scrambled

explanation.surface: A concept about a quirky record of cat songs that moves you unconsciously.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the act rather than naming it: walking while not self-aware is sleepwalking.
explanation.definitionFit: Noctambulation is sleepwalking: walking about at night while asleep and unaware of it.
